Subject: On‑prem bastion + egress pattern: Terraform/Helm/Ansible convergence review

Hi Priya / Ken —

Thanks for the walk through yesterday. Per our call, I sketched a convergence plan that standardizes how your operations team will manage: (1) bastion jump hosts, (2) egress/NAT behavior for model serving subnets, and (3) the CI gate for Terraform + Helm + Ansible artifacts. Attached is a small diagram and an implementation note (terrahelm-convergence-plan.md).

High‑level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether the preferred bastion model is ephemeral (autoscaled behind ASG) or long‑lived HA pair.
- Confirm outbound egress requirements: allowlist (minimal) vs full outbound per service.
- Approve the proposed CI fraud-safety checks (terraform plan diff enforcement, helm lint + chart policy, ansible playbook check).

Proposed timeline: quick review this week, PR to repo by Friday, CI smoke on the staging VPC next week.

I cc'd Laura and Vivek to loop infra ownership and security review.

Thanks,
Aditya
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bastion-arch-diagram.png, terrahelm-convergence-plan.md

From: Priya Shah <priya@acme-cloud.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On‑prem bastion + egress pattern: Terraform/Helm/Ansible convergence review

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from Acme: 

1) Bastion model: we prefer ephemeral bastions (short‑lived, ASG) because of our compliance rules, but we need a stable access fingerprint for audit tooling (we stamp jump hosts with instance metadata and log their lifecycle).
2) Egress: most services only need HTTPS outbound to our SaaS endpoints and telemetry; model updates require access to our internal container registry and to specific S3 endpoints. We do have a small list of vendor endpoints that must be reachable.
3) CI gating: our security team requires that any terraform that alters NAT/route tables is manually approved (rule in Terraform Cloud), but we can automate the rest.

I'll review the attached plan and ping you with comments by EOD.

—Priya
Sr. Cloud Ops, Acme Cloud

Subject: Re: On‑prem bastion + egress pattern: Terraform/Helm/Ansible convergence review

Thanks all — quick infra/security take: 

- Ephemeral bastions are fine, but we need to ensure bastion instances ship a host‑certificate from a customer KMS (HSM trust) or are registered to customer’s host inventory so audit logs can tie sessions to an owner. For our private deployments we typically recommend instance credential rotation every 24 hours and leverage SSH certs issued by the central CA.
- Egress: agree with Priya — we should build an allowlist by CIDR+FQDN. For Helm charts that configure sidecars which call out externally, ensure those values are validated in the chart policy step (we have a policy shim in the pipeline to check values.yaml hostnames).
- Terraform/CI: add a pre‑merge check that runs a terraform plan and fails when it changes route tables/NAT gateways without a specific tag like "manual-change:true". That meets the 'manual approval for NAT' requirement while keeping the rest automated.

I put three small comments directly in the plan doc (links in related_links). I'll be available for a short call tomorrow morning if we need to walk these constraints into the ops runbook.

Laura
Head of Infra Delivery
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: terraform-plan-snippet.txt

Subject: Re: On‑prem bastion + egress pattern: Terraform/Helm/Ansible convergence review

Quick operational note from Acme side: 

- We can support SSH certs from your CA but to integrate with our session recorder we need the bastion to run the recorder agent (lightweight) at boot. Can your ansible playbook add that step?
- For container registry pull access we will provide a role‑bound short lived token per cluster; we will share the token exchange endpoint in a secure vault.

I'll review Laura's comments and Priya's notes and return with a consolidated acceptance matrix by EOD.

—Ken
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below (TL;DR at top):

TL;DR: go ephemeral bastions with SSH certs issued by customer CA, annotate terraform changes that touch NAT/route tables for manual approval, add helm chart policy validation for external hosts, add an Ansible boot step to install the Acme session‑recorder agent.

Action items:
- Aditya: open PR that wires the terraform module to require tag "manual-change:true" for route table/NAT edits + add policy check in pipeline (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/892). Due: 2026-11-13.
- Priya / Ken: confirm the token exchange endpoint and session recorder agent package location (Ken to deliver by 2026-11-13).
- Laura: approve the pipeline change and run a canary test on staging VPC (ETA 2026-11-17).
- Vivek / Irene: add the SSH cert rotation job to the ops runbook and a one‑pager for oncall.

Notes: the attached terraform plan snippet highlights the NAT change we expect in the staging run (terraform-plan-snippet.txt). I'm tagging JIRA-OPS-1248 for the approval workflow.

If there are no blocking concerns I will merge the PR on Friday and kick the CI smoke tests against the staging VPC.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.
Aditya
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
